newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gencor mum on QNI takeover talk.
newsitem.headline: Gencor mum on QNI takeover talk.

text.p: South Africa's Gencor Ltd on Tuesday remained silent on speculation in the Australian bourse that it was about to take over Australia's second largest nickel producer QNI Ltd.
"We do not comment on market speculation," a Gencor official told Reuters.
Officials of QNI and Gencor in Australia were in meetings and unavailable for comment.
QNI shares were suspended from trading at the Australian Stock Exchange on Tuesday at the company's request pending an announcement after a board meeting on June 18.
There was also speculation on the price with dealers quoting figures of below A$3.00 to as high as A$3.40. QNI shares closed at A$2.68.
Gencor was trading at 15 cents lower at 19.60 rand on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
Gencor already operates a mining joint venture with QNI in Indonesia.

In a statement earlier this month Gencor said it was evaluating a number of major opportunities, including projects in South Africa and Mozambique, in Venezuela and Brazil, and in Columbia and Australia.
QNI operates the Yabulu refinery near the Queensland coastal city of Townsville.
It produced 26.64 million kg of nickel in 1995/96 (July-June), about three percent of world production, and 1.43 million kg of cobalt.
